title: Chapter 5.  Formation & Identity — Ladakh as a Union Territory

blocks.content: This short chapter consolidates the precise structural facts of Ladakh's creation as a UT on 31 October 2019, providing the essential baseline before the following chapters examine its governance structure and the ongoing statehood/Sixth Schedule debate in detail.

cells: 31 October 2019, under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019
Leh and Kargil (the two districts of the erstwhile Ladakh region of J&K state)
None — directly administered by a Lieutenant Governor appointed by the President of India
Grouped with Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, and DNH&DD as UTs without a Legislative Assembly
NOT currently included — a major, actively pursued political demand (Chapter 7)
LAHDC Leh and LAHDC Kargil continue to function as the region's principal local self-governance bodies (Chapter 6)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Ladakh is one of only 5 Indian UTs without a Legislative Assembly (alongside Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, DNH&DD, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands) — a frequently tested comparative-polity list also covered in the companion GS volumes for those territories.

items: Ladakh UT formed 31 October 2019 under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019; comprises Leh and Kargil districts.
No Legislative Assembly — administered by a Lieutenant Governor.
Not currently under the Sixth Schedule — a major ongoing political demand (see Chapter 7).
